verdict.line: You lose if you stand in melee range past level 2 and eat a Fury-fueled stun chain; you win if you abuse ranged Cannon Stance poke before he hits his stride.

brief.thesis: Renekton's Fury bar is the whole matchup: below 50 Fury his W (Ruthless Predator) is a two-hit stun with moderate damage, but above 50 it becomes a three-hit stun that strips shields and hits for high damage, so the fight you can safely take at 40 Fury is not the fight you can take at 60. Jayce's job is to poke from range in Cannon Stance, deny him easy Fury generation from autos, and only let Hammer Stance E (Thundering Blow) or Q (To the Skies!) commit when his Fury is low or his E (Slice and Dice) is down.

theirWindow.what: He can dash in, land an empowered three-hit W stun that shreds shields, and follow with a big Q heal. Do not trade in melee here; disengage with Q Cannon Stance or kite with E Acceleration Gate.

yourWindow.when: His E (Slice and Dice) on cooldown (16/14.5/13/11.5/10s)
yourWindow.what: He has no gap close, so sit at max range in Cannon Stance and fire Q (Shock Blast) and auto with W (Hyper Charge) attack speed active. This is your highest-value poke window all lane.

start.why: Picked in 95% of games for a reason: the extra damage and sustain let you win early poke exchanges and survive the level 3-5 window where his W stun starts landing.

boots.why: Runs at 52.2% win rate and reduces the physical damage from his autos and W slashes, which matters since he wants to be in your face to generate Fury.

core.why: Builds mana for Muramana scaling while you poke from range with Shock Blast and Hyper Charge autos.
The active haste lets you disengage the instant his Fury crosses 50 and his E dash is up, or close distance when it's down.
Converts your mana pool into the burst damage that makes your poke actually threaten kills, not just chip damage.

situational.when: he's building armor and you need burst to punish his cooldowns
he's stacking armor from Slice and Dice procs or building tanky
the game goes longer and you need sustained DPS plus shred for teamfights

runes.keystoneWhy: Builds stacks from the ranged pokes you're already throwing in Cannon Stance, giving you sustained damage and healing that outlasts his burst-stun pattern without needing to be in melee range.

summoners.why: Run at 50.9% win rate and the highest pick rate (51.8%); Ignite punishes his Q heal from Cull the Meek and secures poke kills before he can sustain back with Fury-boosted healing.

playing.title: Track his Fury before every trade
playing.detail: Below 50 Fury his W is a two-hit stun for moderate damage; above 50 it's a three-hit stun that shreds shields for high damage. Only trade in melee range when his Fury is low.

playing.title: Poke in Cannon Stance by default
playing.detail: Stay at 600 range with Q (Shock Blast) and use W (Hyper Charge) to boost attack speed; this is the form that wins the matchup since he has no ranged answer.

playing.title: Respect his E cooldown, not his position
playing.detail: Slice and Dice is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s on cooldown; if it's up, assume he can dash onto you from 450 range and don't overextend your poke.

playing.title: Swap to Hammer Stance only to punish
playing.detail: Use Q (To the Skies!) to leap in and E (Thundering Blow) to knock him back only when his E is down and his Fury is low, since this is when he can't punish the melee commitment.

playing.title: Use R to answer his all-in on demand
playing.detail: Mercury Cannon/Mercury Hammer swaps on a 6s cooldown, so you can flex between poke and burst mid-fight to match whatever stance he's forcing.

playing.title: Deny Fury by avoiding extended melee
playing.detail: His passive Reign of Anger generates Fury from attacks, faster when he's low HP; minimizing close-range exchanges slows his stun upgrade and his Q heal scaling.

playing.title: Target his all-in window with Ignite
playing.detail: When he commits with W stun or ult, Ignite removes the healing from his Q and R sustain, turning his all-in into a losing trade instead of a bursty kill.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, boots, and summoner spells above reflect measured win rates from current-patch games (2241 head-to-head games, 50.6% Jayce win rate); the Fury-tracking and stance-timing reasoning is my own tactical read, not sourced from win-rate data.
